harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Bootstrapped a 3-member etcd v3.5.17 cluster across node1/node2/node3 (no etcd pre-existed), wrote application keys, then simulated permanent loss of the node3 member (stopped etcd, destroyed its data dir), and performed a proper etcd member replacement: removed the dead member via etcdctl on the surviving quorum, added a fresh member for node3, and started a new etcd instance there with --initial-cluster-state existing. Cluster returned to 3 healthy members with all original keys intact and replicated to the new node3 member. Then ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: rebooted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (preserving quorum throughout), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed etcd health, cluster membership, and application keys fully recovered after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed etcd v3.5.17 static binaries on node1, node2, node3
Created systemd units and opened firewalld ports 2379/2380 on all three nodes
Bootstrapped initial 3-member etcd cluster (node1, node2, node3)
Wrote 4 application keys under /app/... and verified replication to all members including node3
Simulated permanent loss of node3's etcd member: stopped service, deleted /var/lib/etcd data
Confirmed cluster held quorum (2/3) with data intact while node3 was down
Removed dead member (2f32b36352f5e225) via etcdctl member remove
Added new member for node3 via etcdctl member add, reconfigured node3's systemd unit with --initial-cluster-state existing and fresh data dir, started etcd
Verified cluster restored to 3 healthy members (raft index synced) with all original keys present on new node3 member
Captured pre-restart boot_id and etcd/data health baseline on all three nodes
Sequentially rebooted node1, then node2, then node3 (one at a time, quorum preserved), polling until each came back
Verified changed boot_id, etcd active status, cluster health, and full application key set after each of the three restarts

evidence.requirement: Three-member etcd cluster running with application keys (initial setup, since none pre-existed)
evidence.summary: etcd installed, units created, all 3 nodes started and formed a healthy cluster (member list + health + status tables); 4 application keys written under /app/ and confirmed present.

evidence.requirement: node3 member permanently lost, data unrecoverable
evidence.summary: Captured node3's replicated data as baseline, then stopped etcd and rm -rf'd /var/lib/etcd on node3 (irrecoverable), confirmed remaining 2 members retained quorum and full data while node3 endpoint reported connection refused/unhealthy.

evidence.requirement: Replace lost member with a working member on the same node, cluster back to 3 healthy members with keys intact
evidence.summary: Removed dead member ID via etcdctl member remove, added new member via etcdctl member add, started fresh etcd process on node3 with --initial-cluster-state existing; member list shows new ID 9a9cffed52a33628 as 'started', endpoint health/status show all 3 members healthy and synced at raft index 28, and node3 locally returns all 4 original application keys.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 16724682... and etcd/data health captured; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id c64bc3a1... (changed) with uptime 0 min; etcd active, cluster health 3/3, application keys intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f0f8b8e0... captured; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id c17c55b6... (changed) with uptime 0 min; etcd active, cluster health 3/3, application keys intact.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart (post-replacement): healthy baseline, changed boot identity, recovered state and cluster membership
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a8e7c48c... (from post-replacement node) captured; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 34571774... (changed) with uptime 0 min; etcd active, cluster health 3/3, member list shows all 3 members started including new node3 ID, application keys intact.

attempts.summary: Bootstrapped a 3-member etcd v3.5.17 cluster across node1/node2/node3 (no etcd pre-existed), wrote application keys, then simulated permanent loss of the node3 member (stopped etcd, destroyed its data dir), and performed a proper etcd member replacement: removed the dead member via etcdctl on the surviving quorum, added a fresh member for node3, and started a new etcd instance there with --initial-cluster-state existing. Cluster returned to 3 healthy members with all original keys intact and replicated to the new node3 member. Then ran the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: rebooted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (preserving quorum throughout), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed etcd health, cluster membership, and application keys fully recovered after each restart.
